title: Are Heat Pumps Really Worth It In 2026?
summary: A UK solar installer and a heat pump designer argue well-designed heat pumps work in any home, cover sizing, tariffs, solar and the £7,500 grant, and find a bodged new-build install.

assertions.quote: we don't oversize it because that actually drives down efficiency if it's oversized too much and cost too much to buy
That relationship between your radiator sizing and the demand of heat in your house is what dictates if this unit is going to pay back

verdicts.note: Larger emitters allow lower flow temperatures and higher COP, but the electricity-to-gas price ratio is just as decisive.

assertions.quote: they will literally work in any building provided you have double glazing, that's it.
ground source is really expensive. yeah you're talking tens and tens of thousands.
simply switch to many of the heat pump tariffs out there or any of the flexible tariffs, you'll be saving potentially hundreds

verdicts.note: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme has paid £7,500 for air-source heat pumps in England and Wales since October 2023, subject to eligibility.

assertions.quote: it's going to be, um, comparable to a gas boiler in no time at all and also more comfortable and save you money every year

verdicts.note: Prices have fallen in mature markets, but parity with gas boilers in the UK is a forecast, not an observed result.

The authors say heat pump learning rates are not established and UK evidence shows very small or zero price declines so far, possibly masked by inflation, constrained supply or harder homes, so whether prices will fall is open.
